name: Recursive Return-Value Tracing (call-tree evaluation)
recognitionClueHinglish: Recursive function di hai jo kuch compute karke return karti hai, aur poocha hai final return value kya hoga — ye is topic ka sabse bada, sabse default pattern hai (19 me se 8 PYQs).
whatShouldComeToMind: Draw the call tree top to bottom until every branch hits its base case.
Resolve values BOTTOM-UP from the base cases back to the root call.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Identify the base case(s) and their direct return values.
2. Draw the call tree for the specific input given, expanding every recursive call.
3. Starting from the leaves (base cases), compute each node's return value using its recursive formula, working back up to the root.
4. Report the root's final return value.
variationsObserved: Multiple mutually-recursive functions calling each other (fun1 calls fun2 calls fun1...).
Recursion combined with pointer/array arguments (p+1, size-1 style shrinking).
commonTraps: Not fully expanding the call tree before trying to compute — leads to arithmetic errors from skipped levels.
edgeCases: Multiple base cases (e.g., n≤1 returning different values for n=0 vs n=1) — handle each separately.

name: Recursion + Static/Global Variable Combined
recognitionClueHinglish: Recursive function ke andar 'static' ya global variable use ho raha hai, aur wo variable recursive calls ke beech modify ho raha hai — ye combo pattern hai, dono Static-Variable (Programming In C) aur Recursion patterns ka mix.
whatShouldComeToMind: The static/global variable is ONE shared value across ALL levels of the recursion — every recursive call sees the LATEST modified value, not a fresh copy.
Trace the static variable's value change sequentially in call ORDER (not in the tree's return order).
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Draw the call tree as usual.

2. Additionally maintain ONE running value for the static/global variable, updating it at the exact point in the code where each call modifies it (in actual execution order, which interleaves going-down and coming-up phases).
3. Use the current static value whenever a call reads it.
commonTraps: Giving each recursive call its own 'copy' of the static variable — it's shared, not copied.

name: Number of Recursive Calls / Stack Depth Analysis
recognitionClueHinglish: Poocha hai function KITNI BAAR call hota hai (total invocations), ya stack space/depth kitni chahiye — ye counting pattern hai, return VALUE nahi, call COUNT matter karta hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: Set up a small recurrence for call-count: if f(n) calls itself once → linear (n+1 calls); if twice → exponential (~2^n calls).
For stack depth/space: depth = maximum chain of NESTED (not-yet-returned) calls, not total calls.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Determine how many recursive calls each invocation makes (1, 2, or more).
2. If asked for TOTAL calls: set up T(n) = (number of recursive calls per invocation)×T(n-1) + 1, solve/compute for the specific n.
3. If asked for STACK DEPTH/space: this is just the length of the longest single chain of calls (usually = n for typical single-branch-followed recursion), not the total count.
variationsObserved: Recursion inside a while loop (not a classic single-branch call) — still counts as recursive calls, trace the loop+recursion combination carefully.
commonTraps: Confusing TOTAL call count with maximum STACK DEPTH — these are different questions with different answers.

name: Recursive Print-Statement Output Order (before vs after the recursive call)
recognitionClueHinglish: Function me printf/putchar HAI, aur wo recursive call se PEHLE ya BAAD me hai — poocha hai output string/order kya banega. Classic 'print string in reverse using recursion' style question.
whatShouldComeToMind: Code BEFORE the recursive call prints in FORWARD (original) order.
Code AFTER the recursive call prints in REVERSE order (because it executes on the way back UP the call stack, deepest call's after-code runs first).
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Mark every print statement as BEFORE or AFTER the recursive call.
2. For BEFORE-prints: they appear in the output in the SAME order as the original input is processed (forward).
3. For AFTER-prints: they appear in REVERSED order (the deepest/last call's after-print happens first as the stack unwinds).
variationsObserved: Double recursive call before a single print (abc(s+1); abc(s+1); printf(...)) — combines call-count exponential growth with print-order reasoning.
commonTraps: Assuming ALL prints happen in forward order regardless of position relative to the recursive call.

name: Fill-in-the-Blank Recursive Code (base case / recursive step completion)
recognitionClueHinglish: Recursive function ka code incomplete hai (jaise Towers of Hanoi ya Fibonacci with memoization array), aur blanks fill karne hain taaki correctly kaam kare — ye completion pattern hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: Identify the algorithm being implemented FIRST (Towers of Hanoi, memoized Fibonacci, etc.) from context clues (variable names, comments).
The base case blank usually needs the STOPPING condition; the recursive-call blank usually needs the reduced/smaller argument.
conceptsRequired: Common recursive algorithm templates (Towers of Hanoi, memoization)
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Recognize the target algorithm from structure/naming.
2. Fill the base-case blank with the correct termination condition.
3. Fill the recursive-call blank(s) with correctly reduced arguments, matching the known correct algorithm.
commonTraps: Filling a blank that works for a small manual test but doesn't generalize (e.g., off-by-one in the reduced argument).
